# Results — Study 307 (Coffee-Seasonality): does coffee have a tradable harvest/frost calendar? 2000–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly returns of **Arabica coffee
(KC=F)** plus the **13-week T-bill** (^IRX, the cash leg), built from daily closes resampled to
month-end on a verified hole-free grid: 2000-02 → 2026-05, **316 months**. As-of 2026-06-01;
inputs fingerprint `89301021ccad`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Frost premium"? `BUSTED`

The coffee-seasonality folklore says the Brazilian frost window (Jun–Aug, southern-hemisphere winter)
is the bullish leg and the harvest-pressure shoulders (May/Sep) are the bearish leg. The tape says
**neither leg is real**. The frost-minus-harvest spread is **+0.57%/month with t = 0.34** — a coin
flip — and its block-bootstrap 95% CI is **[−3.47%, +4.46%]**, straddling zero by a mile. No
individual calendar month clears even a nominal |t| ≥ 2 (the best is November at t = 1.82, and it has
nothing to do with the frost story). The calendar timer built on the folklore (long Jun–Aug, short
May/Sep, T-bill otherwise) earns **+0.5% CAGR / Sharpe 0.04** against buy-and-hold KC=F's **+3.4% /
Sharpe 0.20** — it gives back essentially all of an already-mediocre commodity's risk-adjusted
return. And the "frost premium" is not just absent, it points the *wrong way* in the pre-2013 half
(frost mean −0.49% vs harvest +1.18%). `NONE`, `MIRAGE`, frost premium `BUSTED`.

## Data stamp

- **Series**: Arabica coffee (KC=F) + T-bill (^IRX) monthly, 2000-02 → 2026-05, **316 months**,
  as-of 2026-06-01, fingerprint `89301021ccad`
- **Construction**: daily closes resampled to month-end (last close of each calendar month). Grid
  asserted hole-free on every read by `fetch_data`. KC=F is price-only (front future, auto-adjusted
  roll-naive) — not a total-return roll index; labeled accordingly.

## Per-month KC=F statistics (one-sample t vs 0, n ≈ 26 each)

| Month | Mean | t (naive) | t (HAC) | n | Signal? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | +1.68% | +1.02 | +1.09 | 26 | No |
| Feb | +0.50% | +0.21 | +0.30 | 27 | No |
| Mar | −0.54% | −0.31 | −0.32 | 27 | No |
| Apr | +1.48% | +0.91 | +1.01 | 27 | No |
| May | −1.29% | −0.62 | −0.66 | 27 | No |
| Jun | −1.18% | −0.65 | −0.71 | 26 | No |
| Jul | +1.22% | +0.82 | +1.23 | 26 | No |
| Aug | +1.25% | +0.62 | +0.64 | 26 | No |
| Sep | +1.07% | +0.64 | +0.84 | 26 | No |
| Oct | −1.10% | −0.59 | −0.85 | 26 | No |
| Nov | +3.84% | +1.82 | +1.70 | 26 | No (nominal only, off-thesis) |
| Dec | +1.61% | +0.98 | +1.00 | 26 | No |

Not a single month clears |t| ≥ 2, naive or HAC. The largest mean (November, +3.84%, t = 1.82) is
not even part of the frost/harvest story and would not survive Bonferroni correction for 12 tests
(α = 0.05/12 ≈ 0.004 ⇒ |t| ≈ 3). Note the folklore's *signs are wrong*: the supposedly bullish frost
month June is the single most negative month (−1.18%).

## Frost vs Harvest spread (the headline)

| | Mean monthly return | n |
|---|---|---|
| Frost (Jun–Aug) | +0.43% | 78 |
| Harvest (May/Sep) | −0.13% | 53 |
| **Spread** | **+0.57%** | — |
| **t-stat (Welch)** | **0.34** | — |
| **Block-bootstrap 95% CI** | **[−3.47%, +4.46%]** | 5000 resamples, 12-month blocks |

The direction is nominally as folklore predicts (frost > harvest) but the magnitude is a rounding
error and the CI swamps it. **The spread is indistinguishable from noise.**

## Sub-period — the frost premium is unstable and sign-flipping

| Period | Frost mean | Harvest mean | t-stat | n_frost | n_harvest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2000–2012 | −0.49% | +1.18% | −0.64 | 39 | 26 |
| 2013–on | +1.35% | −1.40% | +1.26 | 39 | 27 |

In the first half the "frost premium" is *negative* (frost months under-perform harvest months); in
the second half it nominally reverses but still falls short of significance (t = 1.26). A folklore
edge that flips sign across halves of the sample is not an edge.

## Calendar timer vs buy-and-hold

Long Jun–Aug, short May/Sep, T-bill otherwise (calendar-known rule, no execution lag).
Sharpe = excess of T-bill, both legs. Net charges 10 bp one-way × NAV per leg (4 legs/yr).

| | CAGR | Sharpe (excess) | max-DD |
|---|---|---|---|
| frost/harvest timer (gross) | +0.5% | **0.04** | −75% |
| timer (net 10 bp/leg) | +0.1% | 0.02 | −76% |
| buy & hold KC=F | +3.4% | **0.20** | −69% |

The timer destroys the (already poor) buy-and-hold result — Sharpe 0.04 vs 0.20 — and costs only make
it worse. Coffee futures are a high-vol, low-drift price-only series; the calendar rule does not rescue
that, it amplifies the pain by being short during occasional violent frost spikes.

## The honest takeaway

Coffee has the most *romantic* seasonal story on the bench — a single frost in the São Paulo highlands
can double the price overnight — and that is exactly why it fails as a calendar trade: frost is a tail
event, not a calendar event. The frost-minus-harvest spread is t = 0.34 with a CI from −3.5% to +4.5%,
no month is significant, the premium flips sign across sub-periods, and the timer earns Sharpe 0.04
against buy-and-hold's 0.20. `NONE` on the signal, `MIRAGE` as a trade, frost premium `BUSTED`.
